6548.stem: Ella contributes \$1200 per month at the start of each month into an investment which pays interest at $3.6\%$ per annum, compounded monthly.

parts.latex: Show that at the end of the second month, the future value of Ella’s investment will be \$2410.81.

After 18 months, the future value of Ella’s investment will be \$22 226.19.

Beth has a lump sum of \$21 600 which is equivalent to the total of Ella’s contributions. Beth invests her lump sum into the same investment account paying $3.6\%$ per annum, compounded monthly.

How much more than Ella will Beth have in her investment account after 18 months?

solutions.latex:
The monthly rate is $\dfrac{3.6\%}{12}=0.3\%=0.003$. Payments are made at the start of each month, so the first payment earns interest for 2 months and the second for 1 month.
$$\begin{aligned} FV &= 1200(1.003)^2+1200(1.003) \\ &= 1207.2108+1203.60 \\ &= 2410.8108 \\ &\approx \$2410.81 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the future value after 2 months is } \$2410.81$$

Beth's lump sum is invested for 18 months at $0.003$ per month, so her balance is
$$\begin{aligned} FV &= 21\,600(1.003)^{18} \\ &\approx \$22\,796.62 \end{aligned}$$
The difference between Beth's and Ella's balances is
$$\begin{aligned} 22\,796.62-22\,226.19 &= \$570.43 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Beth has } \$570.43 \text{ more than Ella}$$

meta.generated_note: Ella's total contributions 18 x 1200 = 21 600 matches Beth's lump sum.

6556.stem:
Tom has a total of \$80 000 in an investment account earning interest at a rate of $0.6\%$ per month. Each month, immediately after the interest has been paid, Tom withdraws \$1200 from the account.

The amount in the account immediately after the $n$th withdrawal can be determined using the recurrence relation

$$A_n = A_{n-1}(1.006) - 1200$$

where $n = 1, 2, 3, \ldots$ and $A_0 = 80\,000$

parts.latex: Use the recurrence relation to find the amount of money in the account immediately after the third withdrawal.
Calculate the amount of interest earned in the first three months.

solutions.latex:
Apply $A_n=1.006A_{n-1}-1200$ three times, starting from $A_0=80\,000$.
$$\begin{aligned} A_1 &= 80\,000(1.006)-1200 = 79\,280 \\ A_2 &= 79\,280(1.006)-1200 = 78\,555.68 \\ A_3 &= 78\,555.68(1.006)-1200 \approx 77\,827.01 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{after the third withdrawal the account holds } \$77\,827.01$$
criteria: Correctly finds $A_1$ and $A_2$, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Interest earned $=$ (final balance) $+$ (total withdrawn) $-$ (starting balance).

Total withdrawn $=3\times1200=\$3600$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{interest} &= 77\,827.01+3600-80\,000 \\ &= \$1427.01 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{interest earned in the first three months is } \$1427.01$$
criteria: Uses balance, withdrawals and starting amount in a correct relationship, or equivalent merit

6590.stem:
Jacob makes an initial deposit of \$70000 on an investment, earning an interest rate of $0.5\%$ per month. An initial amount of \$800 is made every month.

The amount in the account can be determined by using the recurrence relation

$$A_n=A_{n-1}(1.005)+800$$

parts.latex: Use the recurrence relation to find the amount of money in the account after the third deposit.
Calculate the amount of interest earned in the first three months.

solutions.latex:
Apply the recurrence relation three times, starting from $A_0 = 70000$.

$$\begin{aligned} A_1 &= 70000(1.005) + 800 = 71150 \\ A_2 &= 71150(1.005) + 800 = 72305.75 \\ A_3 &= 72305.75(1.005) + 800 = 73467.2788\ldots \end{aligned}$$

Interest is the final amount less the total deposited.

$$\text{Amount deposited} = 70000 + (800 \times 3) = 72400$$

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Interest} &= 73467.2788 - 72400 \\ &= \$1067.2788\ldots \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the total deposited, or equivalent merit

6704.stem:
Adam makes an initial deposit of \$5000 on an investment taken out over one year at a rate of $7.2\%$ per annum compounded quarterly, and an additional deposit of \$200 is made each quarter.

The amount in the account immediately after the $n$th deposit can be determined using the recurrence relation

$$A_{n+1} = A_n(1 + r) + 200$$

Where $n = 1, 2, 3, \dots$ and $A_0 = 5000$

$A_{n+1}$ is the value of the loan after $(n+1)$ repayments

$A_n$ is the value of the loan after $n$ repayments

$r$ is the rate of interest.

parts.latex: Find the value of $r$ correct to two significant figures.
Use the recurrence relation to find the amount of money in the account immediately after the second deposit.

solutions.latex:
The quarterly rate is the annual rate divided by $4$.
$$\begin{aligned} r &= 0.072 \div 4 \\ &= 0.018 \end{aligned}$$

Apply $A_{n+1} = A_n(1 + r) + 200$ with $r = 0.018$ and $A_0=5000$.

After the first deposit:
$$A_1 = 5000(1 + 0.018) + 200 = 5290$$
After the second deposit:
$$A_2 = 5290(1 + 0.018) + 200 = 5585.22$$
Therefore the amount is $\$5585.22$.
criteria: Correct amount after first deposit, or equivalent merit
